description.description: A 3D simulation showing a sequence of frames involving horseshoe magnets and a bullet. Frame 1 shows a long row of 100 horseshoe magnets on stands. Frame 2 shows a character in a jumpsuit aiming a revolver at the row of magnets; a 9mm bullet has just been fired. Frame 3 is a close-up of the bullet flying past the red 'North' pole of the horseshoe magnets. Frame 4 shows a head-on perspective looking down the tunnel created by the magnets, with the bullet traveling through the center.
description.ocrText: SUBSCRIBE G 3D VISUAL 100 Magnets A 9Mm Bullet And Then N N N S S Are Not Magnetic

tweetMedia.transcription: What happens if you fire a bullet through 100 magnets? Most people think the bullet would slow down after passing a few magnets and then eventually stick to one of them. But that's not actually what would happen. A 9mm bullet travels at around 1,200 feet per second and most bullets are not magnetic at all. So instead of getting stuck, the bullet would fly straight through all 100 magnets with almost no change in speed or direction.
